# Purpose and scope

Low-pH viral inactivation is the first dedicated viral clearance step in the A-Mab
purification train, and it is a hold and not a separation. The Protein A eluate is titrated
to a low pH, held for a defined time at a controlled temperature, and then neutralised
before cation exchange. The step carries the largest single contribution to the enveloped
virus clearance claimed for the drug substance, and its operating pH is bounded on both
sides, because inactivation becomes incomplete as the pH rises and the antibody aggregates
as the pH falls.

This plan defines the process characterization study for the step, and it states what will
be studied, at what scale, how the data will be analysed, and the criteria against which the
executed study will be judged. It is written before any characterization data exist, so it
records intentions and decision rules, and the results, the parameter classifications and
the operating region will all be reported in PCR-006.

The study covers the parameters in @tbl-params over the ranges given there, of which
`{python} f"{n_mv:d}"` (inactivation pH, hold time and temperature) will be studied in a
multivariate design and `{python} f"{n_uv:d}"` will be studied univariately (§6.4). The
responses are the XMuLV log reduction factor, the aggregate level of the neutralised pool,
and the acidic charge variant level of the same pool. Product quality runs
and virus spiking runs will be executed on the same qualified scale-down model, within the
framework of ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a] and the lifecycle approach to process validation
[@fda2011].

Three limits on the scope are set here. Minute virus of mice is not inactivated at low pH,
so this step is credited with enveloped virus clearance only, and the parvovirus claim rests
on anion exchange and virus filtration (PCR-008 and PCR-009). Host cell protein precipitates
during the hold in platform experience, but the extent varies between runs, so no host cell
protein clearance will be claimed here and the Protein A pool level will be carried forward
as the input to cation exchange (PCR-007). The step does not on its own satisfy the
cumulative enveloped virus requirement, and the contribution required of it is derived in §7.

# Objectives

The study has five objectives, and each is written as an intention, because no
characterization data exist at the time of approval.

(i) To quantify the effect of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature on XMuLV log
reduction, on pool aggregate and on acidic charge variants, over the ranges in @tbl-params.

(ii) To fit a response-surface model for each response and to define the multivariate
operating region in which every acceptance criterion in @tbl-accept is met at the same time.

(iii) To determine a proven acceptable range for each parameter against each attribute it
governs, both at the set-point and with the other parameters varying within their normal
operating ranges (§8).

(iv) To generate the evidence needed to classify each parameter under SOP-4001, noting that
the classifications themselves are assigned in PCR-006 and not in this plan.

(v) To justify the Stage 2 operating ranges and in-process controls for the step, and to
supply its clearance contribution to the cumulative viral safety claim consolidated in
PCMR-001.

Objectives (i) to (iii) are discharged by the designs in §6 and the analyses in §7 and §8,
whereas objectives (iv) and (v) depend on those outcomes and are discharged in the report.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

The step is a hold, and its position in the train is fixed by the pH of the Protein A
eluate. @tbl-train gives the process train and the principal role of each step. The eluate
leaves Protein A at a low pH already, so the titration to the inactivation set-point is
small, and the pool is neutralised to the cation exchange load condition once the hold is
complete. Mixing to pH homogeneity after acid addition and control of the hold temperature
are the only physical demands the step makes on the vessel.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(process_steps_df())
print()
print(": The A-Mab drug-substance process train and the role of each step. {#tbl-train}")
```

Enveloped viruses are inactivated at low pH by irreversible disruption of the lipid envelope
and of the envelope glycoproteins that mediate entry into the host cell. The mechanism acts
on the virus and not on the antibody, and it does not apply to viruses that have no envelope,
which is why the step is credited for XMuLV and makes no claim for MVM (§1).

Low-pH inactivation has been operated on the Novacyte humanised IgG1 platform for three
earlier products (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab), under conditions that have not changed materially
between them. Prior knowledge from those products applies directly to A-Mab for the
inactivation kinetics, because the mechanism is a property of the virus and is independent of
the product. It does not apply to the acid stability of the molecule, which is product
specific, so the lower pH edge has to be established for A-Mab in this study.

Three mechanistic expectations follow from the platform data, and they frame the design.
Inactivation should be faster at lower pH, at longer hold time and at higher temperature.
Aggregate formation should rise with hold time and with temperature, and should rise steeply
as the pH approaches the acid-unfolding transition of the antibody, while acidic charge
variants should increase slightly across the hold without approaching the drug-substance
limit. The study will confirm or refute each of these expectations.

## Quality attributes in scope

The step sets one critical quality attribute and puts two others at risk, and @tbl-cqa gives
the attributes in scope with their acceptance criteria and their assigned criticality.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(CQA_KEYS))
print()
print(": Quality attributes in scope for the low-pH viral inactivation step. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

Enveloped virus clearance is of very high criticality and is the attribute the step exists to
deliver. Aggregate is of high criticality and is formed at this step and not cleared by it,
so the hold has to be shown not to raise aggregate beyond the drug-substance limit. Acidic
charge variants are of very low criticality and are monitored as a guard on acid exposure.
Criticality follows the assessment recorded in RA-001, in which the Tool #1 score is the
product of clinical impact and uncertainty, attributes scored high or very high are treated
as critical, and criticality is treated as a continuum and not as a binary label [@ichq9;
@amab2009].

Enveloped virus clearance is cumulative across the process and is not delivered here alone.
Anion exchange and small-virus retentive filtration each contribute an independent reduction
by a different mechanism, and those contributions are characterized in PCR-008 and PCR-009,
with the cumulative claim consolidated in PCMR-001. The contribution required of this step is
the cumulative requirement less the clearance credited to the other two steps, and §7 gives
the resulting criterion.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

RA-001 ranked the parameters of this step on their potential effect on the attributes in
@tbl-cqa and on their potential to interact with each other, and the
`{python} f"{n_mv:d}"` highest ranked parameters were assigned to a multivariate study while
A-Mab concentration was assigned to a univariate study. @tbl-params carries that assignment.

Inactivation pH ranks highest on both scales. It drives the inactivation kinetics directly,
it drives acid-induced aggregation directly, and the two effects run in opposite directions,
so its acceptable range cannot be set from either response on its own. That two-sided
dependence is why pH receives the most stringent treatment of any parameter in the step. Hold
time and temperature act on the same kinetics as pH, which is where the interaction risk
lies, since a short hold may be sufficient at the low end of the pH range and insufficient at
the high end. Temperature acts on aggregation as well, so it appears in both mechanisms.

A-Mab concentration ranked low on both scales. Virus inactivation at fixed pH is a
solution-phase reaction whose rate does not depend on the antibody concentration over the
range in @tbl-params, and platform data show little or no effect on aggregate across the same
range. A fourth factor would also expand a design that has to be executed under containment
with spiked virus, at a cost the risk ranking does not justify. The parameter will still be
studied across its full range (§6.4) and will still be classified in PCR-006, whatever the
outcome.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The scale-down model is a jacketed hold vessel with overhead mixing, titration by controlled
acid addition, and continuous recording of pH and temperature. The step has no
scale-dependent separation mechanism, so the model is matched to the commercial step on the
variables that govern the outcome: the acid addition profile, the time to pH homogeneity
after addition, the hold temperature and its control tolerance, and the neutralisation
profile. Volume is not itself a scaling variable here, because inactivation is a
solution-phase reaction in a homogeneous vessel.

The model will be qualified under SOP-1001 before any characterization run is executed.
Qualification will compare the model against at-scale platform records for time to pH
homogeneity, hold temperature profile, pool aggregate at the end of the hold, and the
condition of the neutralised pool. The qualification record will be summarised in PCR-006 and
filed against SOP-1001, and characterization runs will not begin until the model has been
qualified, because every conclusion of this study is applied directly to the commercial-scale
step.

Two configurations of the same model will be used. Unspiked runs generate the product-quality
responses, and spiked runs generate the XMuLV log reduction factor and are executed in a
containment laboratory, on material drawn from the same Protein A pool as the matching
unspiked run. ICH Q5A(R2) requires that the spiked small-scale model represents the
manufacturing step and that the spike does not itself alter it [@ichq5a]. The volume of virus
stock added will therefore be held to a small fraction of the pool volume, and the pH and
conductivity of the pool will be recorded before and after spiking.

Centre-point runs are replicated in both designs (§6), and their variation is the pure-error
term against which lack of fit will be tested, as well as a measure of the reproducibility of
the whole procedure, from titration through to assay.

## Operation

Each run will follow SOP-2009. The Protein A pool is adjusted to the target inactivation pH
by addition of acid with mixing, the pH is confirmed on an independent probe, and the hold
starts once the target is reached. The pool is held at the target temperature for the
specified time, then neutralised to the cation exchange load pH with base, and filtered.

The input to the step is the Protein A pool characterized in PCR-005. Its aggregate level,
protein concentration and pH are feed attributes of this step and not parameters of it.
Buffer identity, acid and base molarity, filter type and vessel material are controlled to
platform specification and are not characterized here. A-Mab concentration is the one feed
attribute that will be varied deliberately (§6.4).

## Analytical methods

@tbl-amv lists the validated methods that will generate the responses. XMuLV infectivity will
be measured as a TCID50 titre under AMV-3017, and the log reduction factor is the difference
between the titre of the spiked load and the titre of the held pool, each corrected for
volume. Size variants will be measured by SEC under AMV-3011. Charge variants will be
measured by imaged capillary isoelectric focusing under AMV-3013.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=[], amvs=VIRAL_INACT_AMV_REFS))
print()
print(": Validated analytical methods for the study responses. {#tbl-amv}")
```

The precision of the infectivity assay bounds what the design can resolve. AMV-3017 reports
an intermediate precision of `{python} f"{amv_3017_precision:g}"` log₁₀ and a quantitation
limit of `{python} f"{amv_3017_loq:g}"` log₁₀ TCID50/mL, and the assay accounts for
`{python} pct(amv_3017_var_frac)` of the observed variance in the response. Differences in
log reduction smaller than the assay precision will not be treated as real, whatever their
p value, and full method performance is held in the validation records listed in @tbl-refs.

## Sampling plan

Unspiked runs will be sampled at the end of the hold, after neutralisation and filtration,
for aggregate and for charge variants, and a sample of the Protein A pool will be retained
from each run, so that the change across the step can be reported and not only the outlet
level.

Spiked runs will be sampled at the start and at the end of the hold for infectivity.
Intermediate samples will be taken during the hold, so that the inactivation kinetics can be
described and so that a run reaching the quantitation limit before the end of the hold can be
identified as such. Cytotoxicity and interference controls will be run at the dilutions used
for the samples, as ICH Q5A(R2) requires [@ichq5a].

Centre-point replication differs between the two designs, since the screening design carries
`{python} f"{n_scr_ctr:d}"` centre points and the response-surface design carries
`{python} f"{n_rsm_ctr:d}"`. Every centre point is a complete run, executed from titration
through to assay, so the replicates capture the variability of the procedure and not only the
variability of the assay.

## Statistical methods

Analysis will follow SOP-1002, and each factor is coded so that the edges of its
characterization range are −1 and +1. The coded centre is the midpoint of that range, and it
does not coincide with the set-point for any of the multivariate parameters, so predictions
at the set-point will be made at the coded values of the set-points given in @tbl-params.

The screening design will be analysed by ordinary least squares with main effects and
two-factor interactions. An effect is reported as twice the coded coefficient, so it is the
change in the response across the whole studied range of that factor, and significance will
be judged at α = 0.05.

The screening analysis identifies which factors matter and how they interact, but it is not
the predictive model. The response-surface model is the predictive model, and it is the basis
of the operating region (§7) and of the proven acceptable ranges (§8). The response-surface
design will be analysed as a full quadratic model in the same factors.

Model adequacy will be judged on R², on adjusted R², on predicted R² from the PRESS
statistic, on the model F test, and on an analysis of variance that partitions the residual
variation into lack of fit and pure error. §7 states what follows from each outcome.

Capability at commercial scale will be estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} n_mc` batches, with each parameter drawn across its normal operating range and the
fitted models used to predict the responses, and capability against a one-sided criterion
will be reported as Cpk. A response with no active factor over the ranges studied will be
reported as robust, and its factors will be retained in the knowledge space as evidence of
that robustness.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

@tbl-params gives the parameters, their set-points, the ranges to be studied, the normal
operating ranges and the study type, and @tbl-legend gives the coded letters used for the
multivariate factors in the design matrices in Appendix A and Appendix B.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(plan_params(UO))
print()
print(": Parameters, ranges and study type for the planned characterization. "
      "No classification is assigned in this plan. {#tbl-params}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print()
print(": Coded factor legend for the planned design matrices. {#tbl-legend}")
```

Every studied range is wider than the corresponding normal operating range, because the
purpose of the study is to locate the edges and not to confirm the centre. The rationale for
each range is given below.

The pH range, `{python} rng(PH)`, spans both failure modes. Its lower edge sits just above
the pH at which platform experience shows visible antibody precipitation, so the study can
approach the aggregation edge and still produce material that can be assayed. Its upper edge
sits above the pH at which enveloped virus inactivation is expected to become incomplete
within the hold times studied. The normal operating range, `{python} nor(PH)`, is narrow and
lies well inside both edges. The set-point is pH `{python} sp(PH)`.

The hold time range, `{python} rng(HOLD)` `{python} unit(HOLD)`, starts at the shortest hold
that will be permitted at commercial scale and extends well beyond the set-point, so that
extended holds caused by equipment or scheduling delays fall inside characterized territory.
The upper edge is the condition of greatest acid exposure, and so the worst case for
aggregate and for charge variants.

The temperature range, `{python} rng(TEMP)` `{python} unit(TEMP)`, spans the ambient
conditions of the manufacturing suite and brackets the control tolerance of the hold vessel.
The low edge is the worst case for inactivation and the high edge is the worst case for
aggregate, so both edges of this range are informative.

The A-Mab concentration range, `{python} rng(CONC)` `{python} unit(CONC)`, covers the pool
concentrations expected from Protein A across that step's own characterized load range
(PCR-005). Its normal operating range and its studied range are the same, because the step
imposes no control on the concentration it receives.

## Screening design

The screening design is a two-level full factorial in the multivariate factors with
`{python} f"{n_scr_ctr:d}"` centre points, giving `{python} f"{n_scr:d}"` runs in total, and
the run order will be randomised. The design estimates all `{python} f"{n_scr_fac:d}"`
factorial combinations, so every main effect and every two-factor interaction is estimated
without aliasing, which is what the interaction risk identified in §4.3 requires. The planned
coded matrix is given in Appendix A.

The screening design carries no axial points, so it cannot estimate curvature in any single
factor. The centre points will detect curvature as a lack of fit, but they cannot attribute
it to one factor, which is the reason for the response-surface design and the reason the
screening effects will be reported as an identification of the active factors and not as a
predictive model.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface design is a face-centred central composite in the same factors,
comprising `{python} f"{n_rsm_fac:d}"` factorial points, `{python} f"{n_rsm_ax:d}"` axial
points and `{python} f"{n_rsm_ctr:d}"` centre replicates, giving `{python} f"{n_rsm:d}"` runs
in total. The planned coded matrix is given in Appendix B.

The axial points are placed on the faces of the cube and not outside it, since a rotatable
design would place them beyond the coded edges, which for pH would mean running below the
precipitation threshold and above the pH at which inactivation is expected to fail. The
face-centred form keeps every run inside the characterization ranges in @tbl-params, at the
cost of a less precise estimate of the pure quadratic terms. That cost is accepted here,
because the edges of the pH range are physically meaningful limits and not arbitrary ones.

## Univariate assessment

A-Mab concentration will be studied one factor at a time, at the low edge, the set-point and
the high edge of the range in @tbl-params, with pH, hold time and temperature held at their
set-points. Both spiked and unspiked runs will be executed at each level.

The parameter is excluded from the multivariate design for the reasons given in §4.3, and the
univariate result is informative either way. If no effect is found, the parameter will be
classified accordingly in PCR-006 and its studied range will be retained in the knowledge
space as evidence that the step is insensitive to it. If an effect is found, the multivariate
design will be augmented before any operating region is declared.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

@tbl-accept gives the acceptance criterion for each response together with the basis of that
criterion. The charge variant criterion is a drug-substance specification applied at the
outlet of the step, because no later step changes that attribute enough to matter. The
aggregate criterion is an in-process limit, because low pH holding forms aggregate and cation
exchange removes it again, so the pool is judged on what it hands forward. The viral
criterion is derived, as set out below.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(acc_df)
print()
print(": Acceptance criteria for the study responses, with the basis of each. {#tbl-accept}")
```

The enveloped virus criterion is a step contribution and not a cumulative figure. The
drug-substance requirement is a cumulative XMuLV reduction of at least
`{python} f"{xmulv_cum_req:g}"` log₁₀ across the process, and anion exchange and small-virus
retentive filtration are credited with `{python} f"{xmulv_other:.2f}"` log₁₀ between them
under the modular clearance approach, in which each step is spiked and evaluated
independently of the others [@ichq5a; @amab2009]. This step must therefore achieve at least
`{python} f"{xmulv_floor:.2f}"` log₁₀ of XMuLV reduction across the operating region.

The clearance claim will be framed conservatively in three ways. The claim made for the step
will be the reduction demonstrated at the worst case of the operating region, which is the
combination of the highest pH, the shortest hold and the lowest temperature, and not the mean
at the set-point. A run in which the held pool falls to the quantitation limit of AMV-3017
will be reported as a limit value, and the reduction will not be extrapolated beyond it.
Inactivation will not be extrapolated to hold times shorter than the shortest studied,
because the kinetics are steepest there and a linear extrapolation would overstate the
clearance.

The product-quality criteria apply to the neutralised pool, where aggregate must be at or
below `{python} f"{agg_max:g}"` % HMW and acidic charge variants must lie between
`{python} f"{acid_lo:g}"` % and `{python} f"{acid_hi:g}"` %. Both are drug-substance
specifications. Applying them at the outlet of this step is deliberately conservative,
because cation exchange reduces aggregate downstream of it (PCR-007). A run that exceeds
either limit defines an edge of failure and will be reported as one.

Model adequacy decides what the operating region may be built on. A response whose
response-surface model shows a significant lack of fit against pure error at α = 0.05 will
not be used to define the region, and the region will then be set from the responses whose
models are adequate, together with the univariate data, with the shortfall stated plainly in
PCR-006. A response with no significant factor effect will be reported as robust over the
ranges studied, and its acceptance will be shown from the observed values and not from a
model.

The operating region will be declared as the set of parameter combinations at which every
criterion in @tbl-accept is met at the same time. It will be evaluated from the fitted
response-surface models with the remaining parameters varying within their normal operating
ranges, and not from the mean prediction alone. A model of mean response gives roughly even
odds of meeting a limit at its own boundary, so a region drawn on the mean surface would not
support the assurance that the viral criterion requires.

The pH criterion is two-sided, and it is the decisive one for this step, with its upper edge
set by the log reduction criterion and its lower edge by the aggregate criterion. The study
passes on pH only if those two edges leave an interval that contains the set-point and the
whole normal operating range in @tbl-params, with margin on both sides. If they do not, no
operating range for pH will be declared from this data set, the set-point and the normal
operating range will be reset under change control, and the affected part of the study will
be re-executed.

The study will be accepted as executed when four conditions hold. Every designed run in
Appendix A and Appendix B has been executed, or its omission has been justified and assessed
for impact. The centre-point variation is consistent with the precision of the methods in
@tbl-amv, and every spiked run carries passing cytotoxicity and interference controls. Any
departure from this plan has been recorded, investigated, assessed for its effect on the
conclusions and reported in PCR-006.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis)

The operating region is multivariate, and it will be complemented by a proven acceptable
range for each parameter against each attribute that parameter governs. The acceptance basis
is the one already given in @tbl-accept: aggregate and acidic charge variants are judged
against their drug-substance specifications, and XMuLV reduction is judged against the step
contribution derived in §7.

Two analyses will be run for each pairing of parameter and attribute. The first holds the
other parameters at their set-points and scans the parameter of interest across its
characterization range. The second varies the other parameters within their normal operating
ranges, by Monte-Carlo sampling of the fitted response-surface model, and requires the
criterion to be met across that variation, which makes it the reported default, because it is
the condition under which the step will actually be operated.

The decision rule is the same for both analyses. The proven acceptable range is the
contiguous interval of the parameter, inside its characterization range, that contains the
set-point and over which the attribute stays within acceptance. Where that interval covers
the whole characterization range, the parameter is proven acceptable across everything that
was studied, and no claim will be made beyond it. Where the propagated analysis gives a
narrower interval than the set-point analysis, the attribute that binds it will be named,
together with the margin that remains to the set-point.

Each governed attribute will be reported with a table of the characterization range and both
proven acceptable ranges, for every parameter, and with a two-panel figure for the parameter
that governs it. The panels carry the set-point analysis and the propagated analysis, and
each shows the parameter on the horizontal axis and the response on the vertical axis, with
the acceptance limit drawn, the acceptable region shaded green, and the set-point and the
normal operating range marked.

A proven acceptable range and the operating region are not the same claim, and PCR-006 will
keep them apart. A proven acceptable range is a statement about one parameter, and the
operating region is a statement about the parameters together. Where every parameter turns
out to be proven acceptable across its whole characterization range, the binding constraint
on operation is the corner of the multivariate region and not any single range. Both are
bounded by the ranges in @tbl-params and by the fitted models, and neither will be claimed
outside them.

# Data management and integrity

Data will be recorded and retained in accordance with ALCOA+ principles. Run execution will
be recorded in the electronic laboratory notebook against SOP-2009, with process data
captured from the vessel control system, and analytical results will be recorded in the
laboratory information management system under the method identifiers in @tbl-amv.

Raw data, the fitted models and the analysis scripts will be retained together, so that every
reported value can be traced back to the run that produced it. The statistical analysis will
be reviewed independently by Statistics before the report is issued, and any change to this
plan after approval requires a documented amendment approved by the functions in @tbl-appr.

# Roles and responsibilities

@tbl-roles assigns the functions involved in the study. MSAT owns this plan and the report,
Statistics owns the design and the analysis and is accountable for the operating region and
the proven acceptable ranges, and Quality Assurance approves the plan before execution
begins.

| Function | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Manufacturing Science and Technology | Owns the plan and the report; qualifies the scale-down model |
| Process Development | Executes the unspiked characterization runs and the univariate assessment |
| Contract virology laboratory | Executes the spiked runs under Novacyte oversight |
| Analytical Development | Releases analytical data against the validated methods |
| Statistics | Owns the design, the analysis and the model adequacy assessment |
| Quality Assurance | Approves the plan, the deviations and the report |

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-006, and @tbl-phase gives the sequence of work. No
calendar dates are fixed here, and each phase begins once the preceding phase has been
reviewed and released.

| Phase | Content | Prerequisite |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scale-down model qualification against at-scale platform records | Approval of this plan |
| 2 | Screening design, unspiked and spiked | Qualified scale-down model |
| 3 | Response-surface design, unspiked and spiked | Screening result reviewed |
| 4 | Univariate assessment of A-Mab concentration | Qualified scale-down model |
| 5 | Analysis, operating region and proven acceptable ranges | Phases 2 to 4 complete |
| 6 | Issue of PCR-006 | Analysis reviewed by Statistics |

: Planned phase sequence for the study. {#tbl-phase}

Scale-down model qualification precedes every characterization run. Screening precedes the
response-surface study, because the response-surface factors are confirmed by the screening
result. The univariate assessment may run in parallel with either. Within each
design the spiked runs follow the matching unspiked runs, so that a run failing a
product-quality criterion is known before virus is committed to it.

# Risks and assumptions

Four risks to the study are recognised, and each carries a mitigation that is part of the
plan.

The scale-down model may not represent the commercial hold. The step has no separation
mechanism, which makes the model simpler to justify than a chromatography model, but
titration and mixing are scale dependent, and the model will be qualified on those variables
before execution (§5.1).

The spiked model may not represent the unspiked step. Virus stock carries cell culture matrix
into the pool, and at high spike volumes it can shift the pH or the conductivity of the pool,
so the spike volume will be held small and the pool condition will be recorded before and
after spiking.

The infectivity assay may lose resolution to matrix cytotoxicity. A low-pH antibody pool is
cytotoxic to the indicator cells at low dilution, and the higher dilution needed to avoid
this costs resolution at the top of the reduction range. Cytotoxicity controls form part of
every spiked run. A run that loses resolution will be reported as a limit value (§7).

The feed may not span the states the step will meet at scale. The input is the Protein A
pool, whose own characterization is reported in PCR-005, and only its protein concentration
is varied deliberately here, so feed states beyond that variation are covered by the input
controls agreed with PCR-005 and not by this study.

Three assumptions are made explicit. The inactivation mechanism is a property of the virus
envelope and transfers from the platform products to A-Mab, whereas the acid stability of the
antibody does not transfer and is characterized here (§4.1). XMuLV is a conservative model
virus for the enveloped viruses of concern under ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a]. The neutralised pool
is the input to cation exchange, and no host cell protein clearance is credited to this step
(§1).

# Approvals

This plan takes effect once it has been approved by the functions listed in @tbl-appr, and
execution may not begin before that approval. Amendments after approval follow the change
control route described in §9 and are approved by the same functions.
